01.r: Opens the standing terms that will apply at every harvest.
01.n: A form that looks forward: 'and it shall be'. YLT renders it literally as a past, 'hath come to pass'.
t: And it shall come to pass
And it shall come to pass
And it shall come to pass
and it hath come to pass

02.r: Each time the crops come in.
02.n: The word means produce, yield, and the brief's lexicon adds 'income, revenue'. It is plural: every harvest, year after year.

03.r: The people's obligation to the crown.
03.n: The 'you' is plural: Joseph speaks to all the people.

04.r: One fifth of the harvest goes to Pharaoh.
04.n: Gesenius: the ordinal 'fifth', with the feminine often used for 'a fifth part', citing this verse.

05.r: The crown, now owner of the land.

07.n: Literally 'the hands': the brief's lexicon lists 'part, fractional part, share' among the senses of 'hand'. The Hebrew has 'the' here: 'the four hands', the four parts left over.

10.r: Part of the four fifths is kept back to sow the next crop.
10.n: Gesenius: seed, that which is scattered, whether of plants, trees or grain.

11.r: The farmland they now work for Pharaoh.

12.r: Part is kept to live on.
12.n: Gesenius: food, especially corn, grain, provision.

13.r: Widens the share to the rest of the household.
13.n: Literally 'and for whoever': the relative word, with 'for' and 'and'. Our 'are' is English glue for the 'in' clause that follows.

14.r: Everyone living under each man's roof.
14.n: STEPBible tags this occurrence with the sense 'household'.

15.r: Part is kept for the children to eat.
15.n: Literally 'and to eat', an infinitive; we say 'as food' for the sake of English.

16.r: The young children of each household.
16.n: Gesenius: little children, boys and girls, a collective word; he notes that it sometimes extends to the whole family.

_extra.17: αὐτοῖς (to them): added by the Greek translators; nothing in the Hebrew answers to it.
_extra.27: πᾶσιν (all): added by the Greek translators, 'all your houses'.

01.n: The brief's text reads ἱστᾶι, which is likely a garbled ἔσται, 'it shall be', answering the Hebrew.

02.n: γένημα, produce: 'its produce', that is, the land's.

03.n: δώσετε, 'you shall give', from δίδωμι; the brief gives no dictionary form.

04.n: πέμπτον μέρος, 'the fifth part'; the brief's spelling πέρπτον is a misprint of πέμπτον.

07.n: μέρος, part: the Greek gives the sense where the Hebrew says 'hands'.

11.n: γῆ, land: 'seed for the land', where the Hebrew has 'the field'.

14.n: οἶκος, house. The Greek ends here: it has nothing for 'and as food for your little ones'.
